bull_bear.body:
- Corporate net debt declined by 10% YoY to INR 5,725 Cr; net debt across businesses totals INR 11,160 Cr (Housing Finance 2,075, NBFC 1,955, Asset Reconstruction 1,185, Alternative Asset Management 220, Corporate 5,725).
- BVPS at INR 57 (FV INR 1), up 19% YoY.
- Capital ratios stated as well-capitalised: NBFC capital adequacy 27%, Housing Finance 30%, Asset Reconstruction 36%, General Insurance solvency 164%, Life Insurance solvency 189%.
- Surplus liquidity cover maintained for Jul 26 to Jun 27: opening available liquidity INR 6,100 Cr, total inflows INR 11,900 Cr (expected inflows 8,900 plus fresh borrowings 3,000), total outflows INR 12,300 Cr (repayments 7,600 plus disbursements 4,700), closing available liquidity INR 5,700 Cr.
- Deck discusses no dividend or buyback policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Described as 'Diversified with seven high-quality businesses' held under Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd (EFSL): EAAA India Alternatives (Alternative Asset Mgt), Edelweiss Asset Management (Mutual Fund), Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction (EARC), ECL Finance (NBFC), Nido Home Finance (Housing Finance), Zuno General Insurance and Edelweiss Life Insurance.
- EFSL stakes stated per entity: EAAA 96%, EAML 85%, EARC 84%, ECLF 100%, NHFL 100%, ZGIL 100%, ELI 83%.
- Total customer reach increased to 14 Mn, up 30% YoY, with customer assets at INR 2.8 Tn, up 23% YoY.
- Positioned on two structural claims: 'Robust growth in consol PAT and key metrics of operating businesses' and 'Resilient balance sheet with well-capitalised businesses'.
- EAAA claims a full exit from EIYP, 'marking one of the first successful infrastructure yield fund exits by an Indian manager'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Wholesale wind-down] The ECLF wholesale book was successfully wound down to INR 600 Cr in Jun 26 from a peak of INR 18,000 Cr in Mar 19, described as 'down to near zero from a peak of INR 18,000 Cr'.
- [Stake sale] Carlyle's investment in Nido (Home Finance) is progressing with closure expected in September 2026 - a third-party capital event in a 100%-owned subsidiary.
- [Value unlock] EAAA India Alternatives is planned for listing in Q3 FY27; the deck directs readers to a separate detailed business update of EAAA India Alternatives.
- [Restatement] NBFC AUM, gross loan book, GNPA, NNPA and financials for the quarter ended Jun 25 have been restated on account of the merger between ECLF and ERFL.
- [Definitions] The deck's own safe harbour flags that business-wise financials, balance sheet and AUM are reclassified/regrouped on management estimates and may not directly correspond to published data; net debt is gross debt minus high quality liquid assets and excludes CBLO and securitisation liabilities; customer reach includes MF folios, individuals covered under Group Insurance policies for LI and customers serviced since inception for GI.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Edelweiss Financial Services as a diversified financial services holding company with seven high-quality operating businesses - alternative asset management, mutual fund, asset reconstruction, NBFC, housing finance, general insurance and life insurance - now shifting weight toward capital-light asset management while winding down legacy wholesale credit and preparing to unlock value through the EAAA listing and the Carlyle investment in Nido.

open.item: Management expects to sign up one more co-lending partnership on the mortgages space in the current quarter, with the co-lending business meaningfully starting from Q2FY22.
Management expects to add about 1.5 million retail customers across all retail businesses in FY22.
Management does not expect any significant further impairments on the wholesale book and expects positive slippages (impairment releases) from next year (FY22) onwards.
Management guided that FY22 profits will remain muted as the group continues to hold excess liquidity and reinvest in businesses.
Management expects to complete the Edelweiss Wealth Management NCLT demerger and subsequent listing in the next 12 to 15 months.
Management committed to halve the ECL Finance wholesale credit book again over the next two years.
Wholesale real-estate portfolio is profiled 30% at or near OC/completion, 40% to be completed within the next 24 months, and 30% beyond two years.
Company remains committed to the asset-light retail credit model (housing and SME) in partnership with banks, acknowledging FY22 retail credit growth will be slower while the platform is built.
Expensive long-term holdco/group borrowings taken during the crisis are scheduled to start being repaid from 2022 (FY22) through FY23, reducing the liquidity drag.
Mutual Fund business is expected to become significantly profitable (Rs 50-100 crore PAT) from FY25 (2024-2025) onwards.
Management expects the wholesale book to halve over the next two years and almost all of it to come back (be recovered) within four years.
Roughly Rs 3,000 crore of equity embedded in the wholesale book is expected to be released back to the group between FY23 and FY26 for shareholders or reinvestment.
Mutual Fund significant profitability is targeted once AUM crosses Rs 80,000-100,000 crore (from Rs 55,000 crore currently).
Long-term target for Wealth Management revenue mix is broking ~30%, advisory ~30%, and distribution and capital ~20% each.
Given adequate capital and liquidity, management is not actively seeking capital-raising partners for its 100%-owned Asset Management and General Insurance businesses.

wtt.summary: Building track record — 1Q logged, no reconciled verdicts yet.
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and reassuring; management owned the two difficult wholesale/impairment years and framed FY22 as a muted 'bridge' investment year rather than claiming a turnaround already delivered.
